newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima says checking Creditanstalt bid.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima says checking Creditanstalt bid.

text.p: Indications that the race for Austrian privatisation candidate Creditanstalt may be reopened became clearer on Tuesday after the Austrian government said it had to carefully check a bid by a group around EA-Generali.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima told reporters the last minute offer by the Austro-Italian-German consortium was for about half the government's 19.9 million ordinary Creditanstalt shares. In an invitation for tenders last year, the government has called for all-cash bids for the entire package.

"I am bound by the tender invitation and have to check whether the offer formally complies with the tender rules. We haven't even talked about the contents yet," Klima told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
According to Klima, the consortium offered to take on the other half of the government's stake, possibly financing it with a convertible bond issue, and sell it on the market.
The government's holding in Creditanstalt, the country's second biggest bank, is worth about 13.2 billion schillings ($1.3 billion) at current market prices.
A study by JP Morgan, the government's advisor, last year valued the entire stake at about 18 billion schillings, including a five billion schilling premium for obtaining majority control.
Klima said it would take several days until the formal examination of the offer could be concluded.
"I cannot and I will not rule out a new invitation for tenders," he said.

The minister has repeatedly threatened to invite new offers from other potential buyers if the EA-Generali bid, the only proposal that is officially known to have landed on his desk, failed to meet his demands.
